key_people.name: Lisa Campbell (丽莎·坎贝尔)
key_people.title: President
key_people.title_description: CSA President, first woman appointed to lead the agency in a full-time capacity
key_people.description: Canadian lawyer and civil servant, appointed President of CSA in September 2020. Previously served as Associate Deputy Minister at Veterans Affairs Canada and Assistant Deputy Minister of Defence and Marine Procurement. McGill University BA (1988), Dalhousie Law School LLB (1991).

key_people.title: Astronaut

recent_events.title: CSA astronaut Joshua Kutryk assigned to Crew-13 Space Station mission
recent_events.description: CSA announced astronaut Joshua Kutryk will fly to the ISS under NASA Commercial Crew Program Crew-13, launching no earlier than September 2026, becoming the first Canadian to fly under the Commercial Crew Program.
recent_events.impact: Secures continued Canadian human spaceflight presence on the ISS following Artemis II

recent_events.title: CSA and Korea AeroSpace Administration sign space cooperation MOU
recent_events.description: CSA President Lisa Campbell and KASA Administrator Oh Tae-seok signed a Memorandum of Understanding at the 41st Space Symposium, establishing a framework for cooperation in Earth observation, space science, space exploration, and LEO satellite communications.
recent_events.impact: Expands Canada's space cooperation network in the Asia-Pacific region, opening new avenues for bilateral technology exchange

recent_events.title: Artemis II completes historic lunar flyby mission
recent_events.description: CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen and three NASA crewmates splashed down after a nearly 10-day mission around the Moon, setting the record for farthest distance traveled by humans (406,771 km). Hansen became the first Canadian to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
recent_events.impact: Marked Canada as only the second nation to send an astronaut on a lunar mission; validated Canada's C$2.05 billion investment in Canadarm3 and Lunar Gateway

recent_events.title: CSA cancels WildFireSat satellite contract with Spire Global
recent_events.description: CSA terminated for convenience the C$72 million contract awarded to Spire Global Canada in February 2025 to build 10 wildfire-monitoring cubesats. CSA stated it remains committed to delivering wildfire monitoring capability from space by 2029 in partnership with NRCan and ECCC.
recent_events.impact: Delays Canada's dedicated wildfire monitoring satellite capability; CSA plans to re-engage industry stakeholders for alternative approach

recent_events.title: Canada announces historic C$528.5 million increase in ESA investment
recent_events.description: At the SpaceBound 2025 Conference, Minister Melanie Joly announced Canada will invest a total of 407.71 million euros (approximately C$664.6 million) in ESA programs, a tenfold increase, deepening the Canada-ESA cooperation that has existed since 1979.
recent_events.impact: Massive expansion of Canadian space industry access to European space market; strengthens Canada's position as ESA's only non-European cooperating state

core_business: 加拿大太空局（CSA）是加拿大联邦政府负责管理所有民用太空活动的机构，成立于1989年，总部位于魁北克省隆格伊的约翰·查普曼太空中心。CSA的核心使命是促进太空的和平利用与开发，通过科学推进太空知识，确保太空科技为加拿大人民带来社会和经济效益。CSA的三大核心业务领域包括：太空探索（宇航员任务、月球和行星探测、Artemis登月计划、月球门户空间站项目）、太空应用（RADARSAT系列地球观测卫星、卫星数据收集与服务）以及太空科学与技术（Canadarm3新一代太空机械臂、太空技术开发计划STDP）。CSA年度预算在2025-26财年达到创纪录的8.34亿加元，拥有约936名员工。CSA与美国NASA、欧洲航天局（ESA）以及日本JAXA等主要航天机构保持深度合作，是ESA唯一的非欧洲合作成员国。2026年4月，CSA宇航员Jeremy Hansen搭乘Artemis II完成首次绕月飞行，成为加拿大太空探索的里程碑事件。
apec_stance: 加拿大太空局在亚太地区积极拓展太空合作网络。2026年4月，CSA与韩国航空宇宙管理局（KASA）在第41届太空研讨会上签署谅解备忘录，建立地球观测、空间科学、太空探索及低轨卫星通信等领域的双边合作框架。加拿大与日本JAXA长期保持太空合作，曾为日本Astro-H卫星提供加拿大太空计量系统。此外，加拿大还是亚太地区地球观测卫星委员会（CEOS）的积极成员，CSA于2024年10月主办了第38届CEOS全体会议。加拿大虽非传统意义上的APEC太空合作主导国，但通过RADARSAT卫星数据共享、灾难监测国际宪章等机制，为亚太地区的灾害响应、气候监测和海事安全提供了重要的卫星遥感数据支持。2026年联邦政府承诺投入超过2亿加元租赁新斯科舍省航天港发射台，建立本国发射能力，国防部长明确指出加拿大经济中有20%依赖卫星，凸显了太空基础设施对亚太地区安全和贸易的重要性。
